business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Armored Security Personnel Transport Vehicles

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT Act), Act on Reporting and Use of Specified Financial Transaction Information (Financial Transaction Reports Act), Enforcement Decree of the AML/CFT Act, Act on the Establishment of Financial Services Commission, and Act on the Protection of Personal Information. Beneficial ownership identification is mandated under Article 5 of the AML/CFT Act, requiring financial institutions to identify and verify beneficial owners of legal entities, with a threshold of 25% ownership or control.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) or Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a local notary public in the country of origin, followed by Apostille certification issued by the competent authority (e.g., Ministry of Foreign Affairs) of that country, as South Korea is a member of the Hague Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or Certificate of Existence) of the UBO or Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Registry or equivalent government authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a local notary public, then Apostille certification by the competent authority (e.g., Ministry of Foreign Affairs) of the country of origin.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the formation of the Korean entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the UBO or Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the resolution or PoA by a local notary, followed by Apostille certification by the competent authority of the country of origin.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or equivalent constitutional document) of the UBO or Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Registry or legal representative of the UBO/Parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a local notary, then Apostille certification by the competent authority of the country of origin.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the UBO or Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution where the UBO or Parent maintains an account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a local notary, followed by Apostille certification by the competent authority of the country of origin.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the following lists: (1) Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) and the Korean Financial Intelligence Commission (KoFIU); (2) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (3) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List; (4) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (5) Korean government's own sanctions list under the Act on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism; (6) Interpol Red Notices and domestic criminal records. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a continuous basis, and upon any trigger event. Enhanced due diligence is required for high-risk jurisdictions and for any transaction involving defense-related goods. All screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Commercial Registry (i-REG) - Internet Registration System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Hangul (Korean script) for official registration, but an English name may be used as a secondary name. For foreign names, transliteration into Hangul must follow the rules of the National Institute of Korean Language. The name must consist of four tiers: (1) trade name (e.g., Yuhan Hoesa), (2) business purpose (e.g., manufacture of armored vehicles), (3) legal form (e.g., 유한회사 for LLC), and (4) location (e.g., Seoul). The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file an objection with the registry within 14 days of rejection, providing legal grounds and supporting evidence. The registry must respond within 7 days. If the objection is denied, the applicant may appeal to the competent district court within 30 days of the denial. The court will review the case de novo and issue a binding decision. During the appeal, the applicant may request a temporary name reservation extension. All appeals must be filed in writing, with a fee of KRW 10,000 (approx. USD 7.50).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for this industry. The Korean tax authorities and financial institutions require a physical registered office where the company's books and records are maintained, and where the management and operational staff are present. For defense-related manufacturing, a physical presence is mandatory to obtain the necessary licenses and to comply with the Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) requirements. Virtual offices are rejected for high-risk industries due to AML/CFT concerns and the need for on-site inspections.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Presence of physical office space with signage; (2) Availability of original corporate documents and seals; (3) Employment of at least one full-time employee; (4) Maintenance of accounting records and bank statements; (5) Compliance with local zoning and business permits. Risk of unannounced physical inspection: High (80% likelihood) for defense-related entities, as the municipal tax office and the registry may conduct random inspections to verify commercial substance. Inspections may occur within the first year of incorporation and annually thereafter.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 11232, as amended), Title VI, Section 6 (Yuhan Hoesa), Articles 543 through 586, together with the Poongbup Notary Law and the Registration of Corporation Act
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local District Court Registration Office (e.g. Seoul Central District Court Registration Office) supervised by the Supreme Court Administration Office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan) submitted with the Application for Corporation Registration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act; however, because the entity will seek designation as a defense contractor under the Defense Acquisition Program Act, DAPA requires proof of financial soundness, a three-year business plan, and a bank balance certificate. No blocked escrow account is statutorily mandated for general incorporation, but subscriber contributions must be placed in a provisional capital subscription account until the court issues the certificate of registered matters, after which the funds are released to the company’s operating account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, specifically Articles 543 through 586 inclusive, is hereby ratified. The Company shall subscribe to its entire stated share capital in accordance with the capital schedule attached to these minutes, and each subscriber’s contribution shall be paid into a blocked capital deposit account to be opened at a bank duly authorized by the Financial Services Commission. The Board of Directors hereby authorizes the Representative Director and, in his or her absence, the Chief Financial Officer, to execute all instruments, to file the incorporation registration with the local district court registry, to pay all state filing fees and registration taxes, and to obtain the business registration certificate from the National Tax Service. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company is fixed at the address described in the Articles of Incorporation, that such address is designated as the principal place of business, service-of-process address, and statutory seat of the Company, and that the Company is authorized to execute the lease agreement, arrange public utility connections, and display any legally required corporate notices at such address. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following statutory officers are appointed: a Representative Director as chief executive officer, a statutory Auditor, and a Corporate Secretary. Each officer shall assume fiduciary duties under the Commercial Act and shall exercise authority solely in furtherance of the corporate purpose stated in the Articles of Incorporation. The officers are granted full authority to open bank accounts and execute ordinary course contracts, provided that any contract with an interested director or affiliate shall require prior board approval under Article 398 of the Commercial Act, and any defense export transaction shall require the written approval of the compliance officer and a separate board resolution under the Defense Acquisition Program Act. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Representative Director is directed to retain outside counsel for defense industry and export control licensing and to submit an application for designation as a defense contractor to the Defense Acquisition Program Administration immediately upon issuance of the corporation registration certificate. The Board specifically approves the segregation of all proceeds expected from federal government direct wires and diplomatic letters of credit into a dedicated bank sub-account and the application of all anti-money-laundering and counter-financing-of-terrorism procedures required by the Financial Intelligence Unit of Korea. RESOLVED FURTHER, that no production, sale, transfer, or delivery of armored tactical vehicles, prototypes, or ballistic test articles shall occur prior to receipt of the factory establishment registration, the DAPA defense contractor designation, the environmental impact assessment or prior environmental review approval, the civil defense fire safety certificate, and the occupational safety and health clearance. This resolution shall be effective as of the date it is passed and recorded in the minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarized Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public assigned to the Seoul Central District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in Korean in exact compliance with Articles 543 through 556 of the Commercial Act. The instrument must include the corporate name as Yuhan Hoesa, an explicit business purpose covering ISIC 3040, manufacture of armored security personnel transport vehicles, the initial capital schedule showing each subscriber’s cash contribution, the number and par value of shares, the registered office address, and the appointment of directors and auditor. Each incorporator must appear before a Korean notary public, produce government-issued identification, and execute the Articles in the notary’s presence. Non-resident incorporators must submit an apostilled or consular-legalized power of attorney and passport copy, with a Korean translation. The notary verifies capacity and legality, appends a notarial certificate as required under Articles 557 and 558, and issues certified duplicates for court filing. Any corporate purpose deemed unlawful, including unlicensed defense manufacturing, must be amended prior to execution.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all incorporators
Apostilled or consular-legalized power of attorney for non-resident incorporators
Capital subscription plan
Original Articles of Incorporation in Korean, executed and notarized
Certified lease record or property owner consent for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses authentication due to defective corporate purpose or invalid name, convene an extraordinary meeting of incorporators to amend the Articles with not less than a two-thirds vote and resubmit within five business days. If the objection is based on ownership or authority, supply certified corporate resolutions and a clean chain-of-title document; any language query shall be cured by a sworn Korean translation certificate from a licensed translator.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription Deposit and Provisional Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed by the Financial Services Commission and authorized to handle foreign currency deposits for corporate establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional capital subscription account in the name of Yuhan Hoesa under formation. Each subscriber must remit the agreed full cash subscription in KRW or convertible foreign currency to this account. The bank shall conduct customer due diligence and verify the source of funds under the Financial Transaction Reports Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; foreign currency sources must be evidenced by original wire advices. On the subscription deadline, the bank issues a capital deposit certificate stating the total amount held. The funds remain blocked until the district court registration certificate is issued, after which the bank transfers the balance to the company’s newly opened operating account. For defense-related deposits and future proceeds under government direct wires or diplomatic letters of credit, the operating account must support segregation, negative confirmation, and end-use review capabilities.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Passport or identity card of incorporation agent
Bank KYC and AML questionnaire
Original wire transfer receipts from each subscriber
Written consent of directors to open the provisional account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refrains from opening the account because of enhanced due diligence, provide a Singapore-style source-of-wealth statement, audited or notarized financial statements, and a written narrative explaining the defense business model. If the account remains suspended, apply to another licensed foreign exchange bank or submit the matters to the Financial Supervisory Service’s grievance process; any delay may be cured by obtaining the capital certificate through a notarial public deposit account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporation Registration at the Local District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Central District Court Registration Office through the Supreme Court e-Registry system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formal application for incorporation registration to the district court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office. The filing must include the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital deposit certificate, written consents of all directors and the auditor, and proof of payment of court fees, registration tax, and local education surtax. The court registrar examines whether the filing satisfies all formal statutory requirements under Article 553 of the Commercial Act and the Regulations for Registration of Corporation. If the application passes examination, the court issues the Certificate of Registered Matters (deung-gi sa-sang jeung-myeong), at which moment the Yuhan Hoesa becomes a separate legal person with limited liability. Original notarial documents must be presented physically at the court window within seven days after completion of the online submission. The registration process is completed on the same day if the file is routine, but a case number may be assigned and review may extend if the registrar determines that the defense-oriented purpose requires verification of foreign ownership restrictions.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate
Consent of each director and auditor to serve in office
Registration tax and education surtax payment receipt
Representative director’s power of attorney to file the application
Certificate of the corporate seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a provisional suspension notice, the applicant or authorized counsel shall correct the deficiencies within fifteen days by filing amended Articles, fresh consents, or additional identification. Name conflicts shall be cured by adding a numeric corporate identifier to the name. If the registrar requests a legal opinion on the defense scope, engage a Korean lawyer to submit an expedited formal opinion describing authorized activities under ISIC 3040 and the pending DAPA license.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Business Registration Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office of the National Tax Service with jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days from the date of court registration, file the business registration (business owner’s registration) application with the jurisdictional district tax office. The application must submit the court-issued certificate, certified copy of the Articles, the corporate seal certificate, proof of registered office lease, passport or resident registration card of the representative director, and a formal application form specifying the business classification as manufacture of military fighting vehicles under ISIC 3040. The National Tax Service will issue the taxpayer identification number and enter the company on the corporate income tax, VAT, and withholding tax registers. Because the company will engage in exports and government contracts, the tax office should be requested to issue a zero-rated VAT export certificate and to annotate the company as a defense supplier with an FIU high-risk customer profile. The business registration certificate is indispensable for opening operational bank accounts, issuing tax invoices, and signing government procurement contracts.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Matters issued by the court
Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal certificate
Representative director’s identification card
Registered office lease agreement
Business registration application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office suspends the registration because of the high-risk defense classification, attend a consultative meeting and submit a written business plan referencing the DAPA defense designation and the export-control compliance program. If the tax office assigns an incorrect business code, apply for a corrective registration and provide ISIC 3040 and Korea Standard Industrial Classification descriptions. A rejected lease will be cured by submitting the VAT tax invoice for the rental deposit and an updated landlord consent letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Factory Establishment Registration and Defense Contractor Designation under DAPA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) and the competent municipal governor or district office having jurisdiction over the plant site
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an integrated licensing package for the physical manufacturing facility. First, file the factory establishment registration with the local municipal office under the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act, including plot plans, building plans, machinery lists, and proof of site ownership or long-term lease. Simultaneously, submit to DAPA an application for designation as a defense contractor under Article 23 of the Defense Acquisition Program Act, demonstrating capability to manufacture armored security personnel transport vehicles, including ballistic test equipment, welding inspection capability, painting and corrosion-control lines, and security infrastructure. The DAPA investigation team will conduct an on-site inspection, assess the reliability and security clearance of all directors, and review compliance with the Foreign Trade Act and the Protection of Military Secrets Act. The Ministry of Environment may issue a pre-consultation opinion requiring either a full EIA or prior environmental review. All manufacturing operations must remain suspended until the factory registration and defense contractor designation are both approved.
required_dossiers: Business registration certificate from the National Tax Service
Factory site ownership or lease evidence
Architectural and structural floor plans with load calculations
Environmental impact assessment questionnaire or pre-review application
Fire safety design and evacuation plan
Security clearance certificate for all legal representatives
DAPA application form for defense contractor designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DAPA issues a conditional approval with corrective items, the company shall implement the required physical or managerial protections and resubmit within twenty working days. If factory establishment is refused for zoning non-compliance, file an administrative appeal under the Administrative Litigation Act or relocate the factory to a designated industrial complex. If the environmental authority conditions the EIA, the company must submit a revised environmental management plan and secure a performance bond before proceeding.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA), Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE), and the competent municipal governor’s office for factory establishment registration
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factory Establishment Registration (Factory Registration Certificate) and Defense Contractor Designation Certificate under the Defense Acquisition Program Act; additional Specialized Defense Business Permit may be required for armored vehicle manufacturing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MOE) and Korea Environment Corporation (KECO)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act is mandatory for plant sites exceeding 100,000 square meters in area or located within an environmentally sensitive buffer zone, specially protected military area, or watershed protection region. For smaller plants, a Prior Environmental Review (Prior Review of Environmental Impact) is sufficient. Because the facility involves heavy metal machining, surface treatment, painting, ballistic testing, and likely maintenance of military tactical vehicles, the MOE will categorize the project as requiring a full EIA when installed annual production capacity exceeds 250 units or when hazardous chemical storage above threshold quantities is present.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to public waters must comply with the Water Environment Conservation Act: BOD not exceeding 20 mg/L, COD not exceeding 40 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 20 mg/L, total nitrogen not exceeding 20 mg/L, and total phosphorus not exceeding 2 mg/L. Painting and degreasing lines must control VOCs to no more than 20 ppm total volatile organic compounds at the exhaust stack, and activated carbon adsorption or regenerative thermal oxidation shall be installed. Fine dust from abrasive blasting must not exceed 10 mg/Nm³ at the stack. Hazardous waste, including paint sludges, chromium residues, used solvents, and hydraulic oils, must be stored for no more than 35 days, tracked through the Waste Manifest System, and transported only by a licensed hazardous waste carrier to an MOE-approved treatment facility. Boundary noise in industrial districts must not exceed 65 decibels during daytime operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The facility must obtain a Fire Safety Certification issued by the National Fire Agency after inspection of automatic fire suppression systems, hydrants, extinguishers, and smoke exhaust ventilation, together with a Civil Defense shelter approval if the factory employs more than 300 workers. Structural load inspections by a licensed structural engineering firm must certify that floors can support concentrated armored plate storage, welding fixtures, and ballistic impact test rigs. Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA) clearance is required under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, confirming permissible exposure limits for welding fumes, organic solvents, and noise. If any explosives or ammunition are handled, a separate permit from the local police chief must be obtained under the Safety Control of Firearms, Ammunition and Explosives Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea; online portal: HomeTax Service (HomeTax) at hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Korean Yuhan Hoesa (LLC), the entity must apply for a 10-digit Business Registration Number (TIN) with the District Tax Office via HomeTax Service or direct filing. Procedure: (1) incorporate with the Korean Commercial Registration; (2) prepare the Business Registration Application, Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Incorporation, proof of domestic place of business, representative identification, foreign investor identity documents, and lease agreement; (3) file within 20 days of business commencement; (4) the district tax office issues the Business Registration Number which also serves as the VAT registration ID; (5) if the foreign non-resident entity maintains no domestic place of business, a domestic tax representative must be appointed as the statutory agent for tax filings and notifications; (6) after issuance, the entity registers its electronic tax invoice sending channel through the HomeTax Service and obtains digital certificates for e-filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide check-the-box or elective pass-through classification. The Yuhan Hoesa is taxed as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act. Applicable hybrid mismatch rules operate by statute to deny deduction benefits where a payment is deductible in Korea but not included in taxable income in any other jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general minimum turnover threshold triggers registration; every person supplying taxable goods or services in Korea must register for VAT before commencing business. A Simplified Taxpayer regime may apply for businesses with annual revenue below KRW 80,000,000, but VAT registration remains obligatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic Tax Invoice (e-Tax Invoice) issuance is mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses. Issuers must transmit e-Tax Invoice data electronically to the NTS HomeTax system by the day following the supply date. No physical fiscal stamps or pre-clearance approval API is used; however, NTS applies real-time digital risk scoring and post-filing cross-validation. Cash transactions to unregistered consumers are also recorded through the mandatory Cash Receipt System.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods qualifies for 0% VAT where (1) the goods are sold to a foreign buyer and physically exported from Korea; (2) a lawful export declaration is filed and accepted by Korea Customs Service; (3) the exporter retains proof of shipment, customs clearance, and foreign exchange repatriation; and (4) overseas payment is received in the contracted currency through a foreign exchange bank or diplomatic letter of credit. Qualifying exported services, including certain offshore digital/B2B services supplied to non-resident users for use outside Korea, may also be zero-rated if supported by invoicing and foreign exchange evidence demonstrating the overseas supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry / export clearance certificate)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical movement of goods out of Korea
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent bank foreign exchange settlement receipt proving receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If zero-rated export treatment is challenged and the exporter fails to substantiate customs clearance or foreign exchange repatriation, the NTS will reassess VAT at 10% on the export supply. Penalties include an additional tax of 10% of the underpaid VAT for simple underreporting, 20% for gross negligence, and up to 40% for intentional fraudulent declarations, plus a delinquency charge of 0.03% per day on unpaid amounts. Korea Customs Service may also impose penalties for false export declarations. Criminal sanctions may be brought under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for fraudulent export zero-rating, including retroactive clawback of any VAT credits or refunds received.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central monetary authority; the Foreign Exchange Information System operated by the Bank of Korea and the Ministry of Economy and Finance's Foreign Exchange Transaction Regulations under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act govern the approval, declaration, and reporting framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South Korean won is generally convertible for current-account transactions including trade in goods, services, and routine profit remittances, subject to documentary verification and reporting through the Foreign Exchange Information System. For capital-account transactions, including inbound equity injections, loans, and cross-border guarantees, Korea maintains a nominal free-float regime but applies a prior-declaration or approval framework for certain categories under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree. Export proceeds in foreign currency must be collected, deposited, and either surrendered or converted into KRW within a statutory period, typically within 180 days from the export date, with mandatory conversion obligations depending on the currency and settlement terms; if the export proceeds are held in a foreign currency account at a domestic bank, the bank must verify the underlying export documentation and report the transaction. Capital contributions by non-residents require filing of an acquisition of securities report with the Bank of Korea or a designated foreign exchange bank, and the foreign currency must be converted into KRW through a domestic bank before the capital verification certificate is issued. Profit remittances abroad require evidence of retained earnings audited by a registered accounting firm, payment of corporate/withholding taxes, and a remittance report; stringent AML/KYC review by the receiving bank may further delay execution. Surrender of export proceeds and repatriation rules are treated strictly, and any deviation can trigger foreign exchange violation penalties, customs reconciliation audits, and tax investigation. Overall, the regime is functional and transparent for compliant entities, but defense-sector receipts from foreign government clients will attract extra scrutiny regarding end-use certification, sanctioned-party screening, and dual-use or military goods export licensing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must be collected within 180 days from the date of exportation. The mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds is effectively 100% if the exporter intends to use KRW domestically, but the exporter may maintain foreign currency proceeds in a domestic Foreign Currency Deposit Account; however, for those proceeds to be used in domestic payments or to satisfy capital verification, they must be sold to a domestic bank at the market rate and reported through the Foreign Exchange Information System within the prescribed timeline.

Capital Escrow Account and Trade Settlement Account
Export Proceeds Collection Account and Foreign Currency Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: KEB Hana Bank (Hana Bank, KEB Hana Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMIs such as Wise, Revolut Business, or similar offshore digital banks have low to negligible viability as a primary treasury rail for this Korean defense-tactical manufacturing entity because Korea restricts foreign exchange banking services to domestic licensed financial institutions under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. A non-resident digital EMI cannot legally open a won-denominated account directly in the name of the Korean LLC without passing through a domestic bank partnership; moreover, defense-related ISIC 3040 cargo-vehicle manufacturing triggers Defense Acquisition Program Administration licensing, and the banking AML risk tier is High_Risk_Special_License, which requires physical presence of authorized signatories and submission of original certificates of incorporation, statutory director ID, and business license. Digital EMI rails can only be used as ancillary receivables-collection or supplier-payment gateways in limited low-risk jurisdictions outside Korea, but they are not automatically compliant for the mandatory FEIS declarations that domestic treasury operations require.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors or at least one authorized representative with a board resolution must appear physically in-branch for the first onboarding interview at a Korean Tier-1 bank. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not permitted for high-risk manufacturing legal entities, especially for a defense-adjacent LLC with foreign shareholders; however, a consular notarized power of attorney can be used to authorize a resident director or local company secretary to attend the in-branch KYC interview, provided that the POA is apostilled and accompanied by sworn translation into Korean and the original ID documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) is a non-resident individual or foreign holding entity with less than 100% transparent ownership chain and no verifiable source of wealth in Korea
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate registry extract of the parent entity, individual passports or government-issued IDs of every shareholder above 10%, a notarized and apostilled source-of-wealth declaration, three years of audited financial statements of the ultimate parent, a bank reference letter from the parent's home jurisdiction, and a sworn organizational chart signed by the statutory secretary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business scope includes armored military tactical vehicles causing potential dual-use or defense export control review and triggering high-risk special license scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) license or warrant, Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) strategic goods export license or end-user certificate, contract copies with a recognized procuring government or authorized prime contractor, military end-use attestation, and a Gunpowder/Defense Business Registration Certificate if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a foreign shareholder into a Korean LLC may be classified as a foreign direct investment; absence of prior filing with Bank of Korea or designated foreign exchange bank triggers automatic hold and referral to the Foreign Exchange Investigation Unit
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Notification (acquisition of securities) prior-filing receipt from the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency or a designated foreign exchange bank, remittance instruction with purpose code FDI-110/120, the share subscription agreement, the company's certificate of incorporation, and a bank-issued capital verification certificate once funds are received.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction or sanctions exposure risk: Korean banks will reject the relationship if any direct or indirect counterparty, territory, or payment vector touches OFAC/UN/EU-sanctioned jurisdictions, specifically involving military procurement transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A sanctions screening clearance report covering all shareholders, directors, counterparties, and freight forwarders, a signed end-use compliance warrant, full transaction counterparty due diligence files, IP address/ownership logs for any digital systems used, and a letter of undertaking from the CFO confirming no dealings with embargoed states.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 through a correspondent network to the Korean bank's nostro account, with mandatory declaration to the Bank of Korea through the Foreign Exchange Information System within 30 days of the share subscription filing. The remittance purpose code must be either '120 - Acquisition of Securities' or '110 - Establishment of Domestic Corporation' under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transaction Regulations. The foreign investor must execute a Foreign Investment Notification prior to the transfer, deposit the funds in a Foreign Currency Deposit Account, convert to KRW through a licensed domestic bank, and obtain a Certificate of Foreign Currency Deposit or Capital Verification from the bank, confirmed by the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency in the Foreign Investment Information System.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for export of armored tactical vehicles should primarily use SWIFT MT103 for direct wire payments from allied governments, commercial letters of credit (L/C) advised through a Korean negotiating bank with USANCE or AT SIGHT tenors, and documentary collections for established procurement agencies. All outbound wires must include the correct FEIS trade purpose code and a copy of the customs export declaration (Korea Customs Service export receipt) to allow the bank to release the foreign exchange remittance. For defense contracts, payment terms often require a performance guarantee or an advance payment guarantee issued by a domestic bank under a standby L/C; disbursement to foreign suppliers must follow the Korean bank's internal trade-loan approval and the recipient must be screened against UN, US OFAC, and EU sanctions lists before the SWIFT message is released.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Corporate foreign exchange forward contracts with underlying trade receivables or payables, offered by Korean Tier-1 banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with maturities up to one year

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the Korean won may be available offshore but are restricted for onshore Korean corporates; a Korean entity must use deliverable forwards with a licensed bank and document the underlying exposure

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term foreign-currency capital project financing up to the tenor of the underlying defense contract, subject to bank counterparty credit approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Self-Assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, due no later than March 31 of the following year; one-month extension to April 30 available for eligible entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-declaration additional tax of 20% of the assessed corporate income tax; under-reporting additional tax of 10%; negligent/fraudulent non-reporting additional tax of 40%; daily overdue interest at 0.025% per day on unpaid tax; persistent non-compliance can lead to asset seizure, demand for accelerated payment, and judicial strike-off/dissolution of the commercial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Surtax Return and Payment (Provincial/Municipal Surtax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax office (Si/Gun/Gu) through the WETAX local tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the national corporate income tax return; for calendar-year entities, March 31 (or April 30 if the national extension is granted)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local corporate surtax is 10% of the national corporate income tax; failure to file imposes a 3% local additional tax, and late payment interest accrues at 1.2% per month up to 36 months; local authorities can enforce compulsory collection and suspend the business place license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements Filing (when statutory audit applies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via the DART electronic disclosure system; copy to National Tax Service when relied on for tax deductions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the annual general meeting approving financial statements; no later than April 20 for calendar-year companies assuming approval by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in administrative fines of up to KRW 50 million, criminal referral of directors, rejection of the financial statements for tax allowance purposes, and compulsory audit inspection by the FSS; repeat violations trigger designation as a public-interest entity under the External Audit Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Defense Industry Annual Facility, Safety, and License Renewal Return (ISIC 3040)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) and Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal filing due by March 31 of each calendar year for existing licensed defense manufacturers; annual production and quality assurance statement due within 30 days after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a renewed defense manufacturing license triggers administrative revocation, criminal fine of up to KRW 100 million, removal from the DAPA authorized contractor list, and clawback of Special Taxation Act incentives.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership and Shareholder Register Confirmation Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) as part of the annual corporate income tax filing; local tax office for transfer confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 of each year with the annual corporate tax return; any shareholding transfer must be reported within 30 days of completion
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit or updating UBO/ownership details triggers administrative fines up to KRW 20 million under the Financial Information Act; non-resident investors may lose tax treaty benefits; procurement eligibility with DAPA can be suspended.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (Korean External Audit Act), a Yuhan Hoesa must undergo an independent certified public accountant (CPA) audit if, as of the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year, it meets any of: (1) total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.3 million); (2) annual revenue equals or exceeds KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.8 million); or (3) average number of regular employees equals or exceeds 100. In addition, DAPA/MOTIE may mandate a CPA audit for any ISIC 3040 armored tactical vehicle manufacturer awarded a defense contract, irrespective of the size-based thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for all statutorily audited companies; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP / SME Accounting Standards) for non-audited small entities; DAPA procurement audit clauses require K-IFRS-compliant financial statements for any licensed defense supplier.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Yuhan Hoesa must maintain a continuous and accurate register of members and report ultimate beneficial ownership annually through the corporate income tax return (Schedule of Shareholders and Capital Changes) by March 31. Any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be reported to the National Tax Service within 30 days of the transaction; the internal register must be updated on the same date, and for defense-related contracts, the DAPA vendor registration system must be updated within 10 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Registered Charges and Mortgages
Minute Book of General Meetings and Board Meetings
Share Transfer and Ownership Ledger (if shares are issued)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - USD 4,000 per annum for a professional registered office and company secretarial agent in Seoul or Busan
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 - USD 35,000 per annum for a full Korean CPA statutory audit and tax attestation for a mid-cap defense-industrial limited liability company
